text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALES - Algeria bought 100,000 tonnes of Argentine soft wheat late on Tuesday at prices ranging from $158 to $159 per tonne, including cost and freight, European grain traders said. Algeria bought four cargoes of 25,000 tonnes each for shipment in the second half of December, they said.
- A Philippine firm bought 7,500 tonnes of western white wheat from a Japanese commodity house for November shipment. No other details were available.

WHEAT SALES (cont.) - Korea Flour Milling Corp said on Wednesday it bought 16,400 tonnes of U.S. wheat from Japanese trading house Itochu Corp. Early Wednesday, traders said the company had sought 16,700 tonnes of U.S. wheat, but a Korea Flour official corrected later the amount to 16,400 tonnes. The company official said arrival was set to Mokpo.

SOYBEAN SALE - Thai oil crushers bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans at $298 a tonne for prompt shipment, trade sources said. The tender was held on Tuesday. The price for the soybeans was quoted C&F Si Chang, a port in the east of Bangkok.

CORN TENDERS - The Cyprus Grain Commission on Wednesday invited tenders for the supply of one cargo of 18,000 tonnes of maize, with a shipment date of November or December 1996. The tender closes on Tuesday November 5.

- Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group will tender on Friday for one 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. corn, local traders said. The shipment would be for January 26 to February 10 delivery from the U.S. Gulf or February 11-25 from the Pacific Northwest, traders said.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company said Wednesday it was extending until noon (1000 GMT) November 6 the deadline for bids for 30,000 tonnes U.S. or Argentine yellow corn and 30,000 tonnes of soybean, any origin. The old deadline was October 30.
SOYOIL TENDER - The CCC said it was tendering on November 6 for 13,000 tonnes of bulk crude degummed soybean oil for donation to Peru. The oil was slated for Dec 14-30 delivery.
WHEAT TENDER - Pakistan is seeking 200,000 tonnes of U.S. number two or better soft white wheat for Nov 12-30 delivery. Bids will be opened on November 3.

MARKET TALK - The European Union is not trying to prevent exporters from finalising barley sales clinched with Saudi Arabia, but a weaker U.S. dollar limits its scope in granting export subsidies, a European Union grain official said. Some traders, scrambling to deliver barley they have pledged to the Saudis on time, would like the European Union to award higher export subsidies for barley to make up for a fall in the U.S. dollar...Turkey is still inspecting a cargo of 15,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat suspected of carrying ergot fungus, agriculture ministry officials said. The U.S. stopped issuing export certificates for wheat shipments to Turkey on October 18.

MARKET TALK (cont.) - Indonesia will continue to import crude palm oil to ensure sufficient supply ahead of Christmas, the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr, Beddu Amang, head of the state logistics agency BULOG, said. He said the agency would also build up its buffer stock by purchasing 30,000 tonnes of crude palm oil from state-owned plantation, PT Perkebunan Nusantara.
